rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; synthetic validation on the real panel in both models with seven worlds and an oracle check, which showed the test unpowered before any real statistic (Amendment A3); replication on 24 regime-I periods plus the card-level exponent and nine variants; regime III descriptive; two natives (NE27, G51 with NE32/NE33) with their own power; one labelled post hoc check calibrated against three worlds; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run (both build paths), not run.
rationale.faithfulness: The finite-magnet model cannot be tested here: the slope estimator has power 0.00 against alpha = -1 and an oracle has SD 0.45. Real alpha_k is +0.40 / +1.22 with CIs of +-2, likelihood ratio magnet/drift 0.65-0.90. Natives are unpowered. Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D0 E0 F0 G0 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A clear negative on feasibility: finite-size scaling of a slow timescale needs several villages, not one. The post hoc era result (slow mode only at N < 8) is a concrete lead for H81's carrier question, but unconfirmed.

one_line: The 1/N finite-magnet signature of H81's slow mode is not identifiable in one village (power 0.00; real alpha_k +0.40/+1.22, CIs +-2); post hoc, the mode is confined to the N < 8 era.
